entities.summary: Nikolai Alekseevich Voznesensky was a Soviet politician and economic planner who oversaw the running of Gosplan during the German–Soviet War of 1941–1945. A protégé of Andrei Zhdanov, Voznesensky was appointed Deputy Premier in May 1940. He became directly involved in the recovery of production associated with the evacuation of industry eastwards after the start of the war. His 1947 work The Economy of the USSR during World War II records those years. Nikolai Voznesensky was a performers & entertainers from Tula (1903-12-01, Tula–1950-10-01). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to economic history and geopolitics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Voznesensky's work on Gosplan and economic recovery during WWII had a significant impact on Soviet industry and resource allocation, influencing the country's war effort. His record of the USSR's wartime economy remains an important historical document.
